chose: Timeline list renders newest-first as a reversed VIEW over the chronological model (displayRecords), with ui.cursor indexing display order so 0 is always the tip
because: the tail, snapshot and follow pipes all lean on timelineOrder ascending; reversing only at the list surface keeps one canonical order and makes follow = cursor pinned at 0

chose: Streams picker orders by most-recent activity via a new sessionsByRecency helper in journal.ts
because: deriveSessions feeds the settled render too; the recency sort belongs beside the one surface that wants it

chose: Timeline windows by whole cells with a persistent scroll anchor the render reconciles in place; selection slides the window only at the edges
over: keeping renderStreamFrame stateless and deriving the window from the cursor alone
because: cursor-only derivation cannot distinguish 'moved within view' from 'keep the page', and cell heights exist only at layout time (wrap width) — so the render is the one place edge-only sliding can be decided; same inputs still yield the same frame and anchors

chose: New arrivals prepend at the top; when not following (or in a drill-in) the selection is re-found by record identity, not row number
over: letting the cursor keep its index and drift onto a different entry
because: newest-first means every append shifts display indices — index-keeping would yank the reader onto a different record mid-read, the exact yanking the follow pause exists to prevent

chose: Timeline cells clamp to a metadata line plus two wrapped text lines, ellipsized, with a blank rule between cells; the ellipsis rides the second line via clip
over: variable-height cells showing the full text, or keeping one clipped table row
because: full text turns the list into the drill-in and makes paging jumpy; one row crammed when/who/what into a race for the same characters — two lines is enough to recognize an entry, and Enter has the rest
